title: perf: performance canary auto-detection and rollout guards
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: our perf canary system was detecting regressions primarily via static thresholds which produced either noisy alerts or missed small but real regressions. This PR implements an automated detection pipeline using statistical baselineing (rolling-window percentiles + control-chart style detection) and introduces rollout guards that automatically block or roll back model/service rollouts when significant latency or throughput regressions are detected.

What this PR does: 1) adds an adaptive detector service that computes expected distributions for p50/p95 latency and qps per model-route using a 24h rolling window and an exponential decay weight, 2) implements a two-stage alerting rule combining a robust z-score and an asymmetric tolerance band to reduce false positives from transient spikes, 3) plugs detector output into the existing perf-canary orchestrator so canary rollouts evaluate detector verdicts before promoting traffic, 4) implements automatic rollback/fail-open policies configurable by release channel (canary/stage/prod), 5) adds metrics, dashboards and CI perf-e2e checks to validate detector behavior in synthetic regression scenarios, and 6) updates docs and runbooks.

Checklist: - [x] Detector implementation (perf-canary/service/detector.py) - [x] Rollout guard controller (perf-canary/rollout/guard_controller.py) - [x] Integration with canary pipeline and publish/subscribe hook - [x] Unit + integration + perf-e2e tests - [x] Dashboards + alert rules (observability) - [x] Docs + runbook updates - [x] Feature flagged behind config (feature.perf_canary.auto_detect = true)

Notes: This is feature-flagged and off by default for existing customers. There is a migration guide in docs/perf-canary.md and a follow-up change planned to expose finer-grained tolerance configuration per-customer (ENG-4890). The detection parameters are intentionally conservative initially to avoid blocking rollouts for noisy workloads.

Related: ENG-4821 (perf canary improvements), SUP-3241 (customer incident that motivated asymmetric tolerance), design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/perf-canary-auto-detection-design
commits: 6 commits: 1) add adaptive detector core and tests, 2) implement guard controller and GRPC hook, 3) integrate with canary orchestrator and publish detector verdicts, 4) add perf-e2e synthetic scenarios, 5) add dashboards and alert rules, 6) docs and runbook edits
diff_snippets:
@@ perf-canary/service/detector.py +42, +87
+def detect(latency_series, qps_series):
+    # rollup window + exponential decay baseline
+    baseline = compute_rolling_percentiles(latency_series, window=86400, decay=0.95)
+    score = robust_zscore(latency_series[-1], baseline.p95, baseline.iqr)
+    return score > CONFIG.THRESHOLD  # conservative default

@@ perf-canary/rollout/guard_controller.py +10, +64
+class RolloutGuard:
+    def evaluate(canary_context):
+        verdict = detector.query(canary_context.metrics)

@@ infra/ci/perf-canary.yml +1, +30
+jobs:
+  perf-e2e:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - name: run synthetic regression test
+        run: pytest perf-canary/e2e --markers regression --maxfail=1

release_notes: Adds adaptive performance canary detection and rollout guards (feature-flagged). Improves detection of p95 latency and throughput regressions and blocks/promotes rollouts automatically based on configurable policies. Includes dashboards, alert rules, and e2e perf tests.
rollout_policy_summary: Two-stage guard: (1) soft-block — mark canary as failing but allow manual override; (2) hard-block — automatic rollback for production channel when detector shows sustained regression for 3 consecutive evaluation windows. Tolerance is asymmetric and configurable per release channel.
tests_summary: Added unit tests for detector math and thresholds, integration tests for canary integration, and perf-e2e synthetic regression scenarios that validate both detection sensitivity and noise tolerance. Perf-e2e runs in CI as a gated job for canary and staging merges.
monitoring_integrations: prometheus: new metrics and recording rules
pagerduty: soft-block alerts (pagerduty service ID hidden)
notes_for_ops: Feature flagged behind feature.perf_canary.auto_detect. To enable in staging set helm value perfCanary.autoDetect=true and apply alerting rules. Run perf-e2e locally with: pytest perf-canary/e2e --markers regression. Runbook updated in docs/perf-canary.md.
ci_flakiness_notes: Observed one flaky test in earlier runs (test_noisy_restart) — added additional stabilization and reran; CI now green. Perf-e2e intentionally conservative timeouts to reduce CI flakes.
